title: directory
description: runtime -> connector: the router's most recent word about which peers this agent may address, published per instance at <agent-id>/directory.json. amap-spec v3.1.0 DRAFT (spec/contract.md §10). ADVISORY, NEVER AUTHORITATIVE: an address's presence is not a prediction that a submit to it will be accepted, nor its absence a prediction of refusal — authorisation is evaluated by the runtime at submit time and only the result (§4) reports what happened. A runtime MUST NOT read this file back as authorisation; enforcement stays the runtime's own graph check on every message. The file MAY be absent. Runtime-authored: envelope is OPEN at every level per §7's v3.0.0 tolerance rule — a consumer MUST ignore members it does not recognize; emitting an unrecognized member remains producer non-conformance.

router.description: the publishing runtime's own address, one bare addr-spec. Never appears in delegate_to or mail_to.

written_at.description: RFC 3339, the publishing runtime's clock. The only staleness signal a consumer gets; an honest marker, not a freshness guarantee.

delegate_to.description: sorted addresses this agent may task — the authorisation graph transposed for this instance. Always present; empty when the lane is closed. Never this agent's own address, and never who may task THIS agent (an allowlist, withheld by construction).

mail_to.description: sorted addresses on the mutual mail lane. Always present; empty when the lane is closed, which is the normal case for a delegation-only deployment.
